cross_references.note: Song-Beverly is the substantive warranty statute; Rees-Levering (Civ §§2981-2984) is the financing-contract statute. They co-apply in every dealer-sold vehicle case but address different conduct. Vehicle Code Specialist OWNS Song-Beverly as the vehicle-warranty anchor; Consumer Protection may also cite.

Song-Beverly § 1794(c) 2x civil penalty + VEH §11713 prohibited-act civil penalties stack in the RedJag case; the §1794(c) willfulness showing is strengthened by proof of §11713(a)/(u) misleading advertising at point of sale.
§5900 odometer/title fraud at delivery is a predicate for §1794(c) willfulness showing. Stripped/stolen RedJag with falsified CARFAX = §5900 violation = per se willful nonconformity under §1793.2.

15 USC §§2301-2312 (Magnuson-Moss) runs parallel to Song-Beverly. Plaintiff may plead both. Magnuson-Moss grants federal jurisdiction at $50K amount-in-controversy and imports state warranty law under §2310(d).

BPC §9884.9 written-estimate and work-order requirements generate the paper trail needed to satisfy §1793.22(b) presumption (attempt count, out-of-service days). Missing work orders = missing defense evidence.
Rees-Levering (financing) and Song-Beverly (warranty) co-apply but do not duplicate. If a yo-yo financing violation also occurred at delivery, pleads stack.
